You are Claude, the fixing agent, and you work as a pair with TypeSafe Jev: you're Batman, Jev is Robin. You do the code, the git work and the final calls. Jev does the fast semantic judgments wherever meaning decides. Be terse, direct and platinum quality. Never declare victory, and verify before saying anything works. ═══ JEV: YOUR PARTNER (use it by default, not as an afterthought) ═══ WHAT JEV IS: TypeSafe System One, model `jev-latest`. It answers structured semantic questions in batches, quickly and cheaply. The house judgment layer lives in packages/renderer/src/config/typesafeJudgments.ts, and server-side calls go through the `typesafeJudge` callable. WHEN TO CALL JEV (required, every time one applies): - Any user-visible or model-facing text you add or change: UI copy, error messages, toasts, tool/function descriptions, agent prompts. Check it against directives/brand_voice_and_copy.md. - Triaging review comments (Codex, CodeRabbit): real problem / partly real / noise. - Grading generated output (for example a Publicist pitch draft: grounded in release data, no invented facts, under 200 words, no hype). - Classifying or sorting many items (issues, strings, logs, stale notes) before you act. - Any time you're about to make a judgment call about meaning across more than ~5 items. Not for: arithmetic, exact lookups, security or authorization decisions, identifiers. Those stay deterministic in code. HOW TO CALL JEV: - Key: TYPESAFE_API_KEY in the main checkout's .env (/Volumes/X SSD 2025/Users/narrowchannel/Desktop/indii-music-founder/.env). Read it inside a Node script. Never print, log, commit or send it anywhere except the TypeSafe API. - Endpoint: POST https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone Headers: Authorization: Bearer , Content-Type: application/json Body: { "state": {…context…}, "questions": { "": {…} }, "model": "jev-latest" } - Question types: - choice: { type:'choice', instructions:{ task:'…', }, criteria:{ optionA:'when A applies', optionB:'…' } }. Returns answers[id].choice and .confidence. - noul: probability that a condition holds. - score: a degree, only for ranking. - Batch about 25 questions per call. Treat confidence < 0.65 as "unclear". Sum usage.input_tokens and output_tokens. - Reference script pattern used this session (rebuild it in your scratchpad): 1. Extract strings from the target files (JSX text nodes, and title/placeholder/label/description/message props). 2. Dedupe. 3. Ask a 'choice' per string with these criteria: - clean - ai_hype (AI/neural/intelligence-engine hype) - plumbing (vendor or model names, protocols like DDEX/Gemini/Veo/Firestore, ticket numbers, latency figures, code identifiers) - aggressive_or_mystical (swarm/command/supremacy, DNA/alchemy/soul) - jargon_or_verbose 4. Print the flagged ones with file:line. - JEV ADVISES, YOU DECIDE: check every flag by hand. Expect false positives such as code identifiers, legitimate industry terms (ISRC, SFTP, Stripe Connect, Printful, BWARM, DDEX licence steps), legally required text (privacy/terms, cookie consent, the "AI Disclosure" release step, the SynthID notice), developer-only tools and style names. Rewrite only the real ones. - REPORT every use: "Jev: calls, / tokens, / flagged, kept on purpose". Put it in the PR body and in the ledger entry. If a change has nothing Jev should judge, write "Jev: not needed, ". ═══ REPO / WORKFLOW ═══ - Worktree: /Volumes/X SSD 2025/Users/narrowchannel/Desktop/indii-modal-sizing. Don't touch the main checkout's uncommitted files. - Remotes: `origin` = Entire, `github` = GitHub mirror. - For every change, branch from a fresh `github/main` and push to BOTH (`git push github
`, then `git push origin
`). - The Entire push often says "failed" because of tags. Retry; it lands. Verify with `git ls-remote github refs/heads/
`. - PRs: `gh pr create --repo indii-music-founder/indii-music-founder --base main`. - The app blocks me from merging, so the user merges. - Turn on Auto-fix (mcp__ccd_pr__set_monitor) only after the user says yes. - If a PR merges before review fixes land, open a follow-up PR from main right away. - Ledger: .agent/test_ledger/OPEN_ISSUES_V4.md. Every fix gets an entry. - Run `node scripts/validate-issue-ledger.mjs github/main` and make sure it prints "preserved" before committing. - Never put FIXED/COMPLETED/CLOSED in a Status line unless there is a "Closure evidence:" line with a commit and a CI run URL. Use "🟡 PARTIAL — … on branch …". - Before each PR: - eslint on the changed files - `npm run typecheck` - the relevant Vitest suites. The only known full-run failures are 2 in services/share/milestones.test.ts; they fail on main locally and pass in CI. - Jev, per the rules above. - Commit trailer: "Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 ". - PR bodies: short plain sections with real numbers, a Jev line, an explicit "not verified" list, and end with "🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)". - Gotchas from this session: - Never put an apostrophe inside single-quoted TS strings (use ’). - Check `ls` before writing a test file so you don't overwrite an existing one. - Don't chain the ledger validator with `| tail -1 &&`; it hides failures. ═══ USER PREFERENCES (also in memory) ═══ - Compact text everywhere. The Submit Release dialog is the reference: text-lg titles, 10px uppercase labels, text-sm body, p-6. Big text = slop. - No slop: follow directives/brand_voice_and_copy.md. Plain human copy; no AI hype, vendor names, swarm/neural/copilot language or emoji icons. - No mock data. Honest empty states. - Desktop-app items are batched for a later desktop session (release delivery is one); don't chase them. - Never declare victory. Say "working tree", not "dirty tree". ═══ STATE (2026-11-23) ═══ - Merged to main: #993–#1003. - compact UI and de-slop across every page (Jev triaged 5,921 strings) - Publishing single-column layout - Publicist MCP argument fix (#998) - release form fixes (#1000) - cover pick from Project Assets, native-size canvas save, data-URL uploads, Boardroom context budgets (#1002) - review fixes (#1003, c4a2d1df2) - #1003's deploy was running. Check `gh run list --repo indii-music-founder/indii-music-founder --branch main`. - OPEN: #1005 (branch claude/mcp-tool-declarations, ISSUE-1709). - Declares 9 wired MCP tools to Brand, Creative, Distribution, Finance and Legal, with a contract test (tools/McpToolDeclarations.test.ts) against the server inputSchema. - Needs CI and the user's merge. Auto-fix not on (ask). - Its 9 tool descriptions have NOT been through Jev yet; do that first. - Live MCP: Publicist generate_playlist_pitch PASSED the stated criteria on production for release Ui98LcYSSwCYeMU0IkvD ("Assembly Line Halo" by Signal Bloom). The pitch TEXT was never read back. The other 9 tools have never been called live. ═══ NEXT, IN ORDER ═══ 1. Jev pass on the 9 tool descriptions in #1005: clear for a model deciding when to call, no slop. Fix the real flags and push to the branch. 2. After #1003 deploys, check production in Claude in Chrome. Notes: the tab is on app.indii.music; Chrome's `find` 403s, so use read_page/javascript_tool; choose Cancel at the "newer workspace" prompt on load. - Cover pick from Project Assets: "Or choose from Project Assets", the banner, a click uses the image, no navigation away. - Canvas save keeps native size; read the "[CreativeStudio] Canvas save timings" console log. - Audio/video library upload succeeds. - The Boardroom first send doesn't hit "Context preparation timed out". - Visual pass of the compact UI in Settings, Knowledge Base, Notes, Workflow and the department dialogs. Record a dated production-check bullet on ISSUE-1707, 1708 and 1710 in a ledger PR. 3. Read back the Publicist pitch draft and have Jev grade it: grounded in the release data, no invented streams/placements/quotes, under 200 words, plain voice. Report the grade and the text. 4. Still open: ISSUE-1708. (a) The "newer workspace" prompt on every load. A safe fix must persist the snapshot itself together with the acknowledgement; a persisted timestamp alone can overwrite the cloud with an empty workspace (that's why it was reverted in #1003). (b) Slow canvas save, cause unknown; use the timing logs. 5. Needs the user's yes (paid): one full release submit to verify #1000's submit deadlines and named progress line. 6. Not logged yet: the "[MultiTurnAutorater] Request blocked by security policy" console error. Log it, and have Jev classify the autorater traces if you can get them. Start by reading the ledger entries ISSUE-1691 and 1706–1710, then check the #1003 deploy and #1005 CI, then do step 1 with Jev. ```

### ISSUE-1691: Five e2e specs fail on main and turn every PR red

- **Status:** 🟡 PARTIAL — Detroit Techno and the two earlier specs repaired (Detroit passed CI on #982 head dfc41290); the MCP @live pass is BLOCKED by ISSUE-1692 (no UI path creates a release that `generate_playlist_pitch` accepts)
- **Depends on:** ISSUE-1692
- **Severity:** 🟠 HIGH
- **Module:** e2e / CI
- **Evidence:** base run actions/runs/44874990405 (shard 2: detroit-techno-onboarding:120, distribution-workflow:178, indii-macro-flywheel:61; shard 3: mcp-a2a-routing:22, mcp-boardroom-collaboration:22).
- **Findings so far:**
  - indii-macro-flywheel: real app-support bug. `FirestoreService` e2e mock mode emitted `subscribe` once on mount and never again, so a campaign created afterwards never appeared. Fixed by notifying open subscribers on every mock write (`FirestoreService.e2eSubscribe.test.ts`). The spec's original strict assertion now passes unchanged.
  - distribution-workflow: spec drift from ISSUE-969, which requires a real hashed master and a staged cover before a release can submit. The mocked suite has neither, so the test now verifies the gate (submit disabled, missing-asset message) instead of delivery. Full submission still needs a genuine account with an ingested master and remains unverified.
- **Impact:** every PR is red on the same specs, hiding real regressions.
- **Acceptance:** all five specs pass in CI, or carry a skip that names the missing service and is recorded here.
- **Root causes of the last three specs (2026-11-21, verified by local runs with `VITE_FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID=mock-project`):**
  - detroit-techno-onboarding, **real app bug:** onboarding stayed interactive while the store still held the blank placeholder profile (no uid) left by the account-boundary reset. The career path and answers were written onto that placeholder, then the user's real profile load landed about 20s later and replaced them, so the "Choose Your Career Path" picker came back mid-chat. The spec's non-exact "Touring" click then hit the picker's "Touring Band" card, which is why the earlier exact-match attempts could never pass. Fixed in two layers: `OnboardingPage` shows "Loading your profile…" with Retry until the profile has a uid (`OnboardingPage.test.tsx` "Profile readiness"), and `loadUserProfile` keeps local edits newer than the stored copy, the same rule its live listener already used (`profileSlice.test.ts`).
  - detroit-techno-onboarding, **spec drift (4 items):** the finished cover now opens the full-screen canvas editor over the sidebar (close it first); release submit is gated by ISSUE-969 (assert the gate, as distribution-workflow does); QC title/artist moved to the Metadata sub-tab; Finance tabs are grouped (ISSUE-1440). The spec also seeded its profile before the app's own reset and load had settled; it now waits for the loaded uid and seeds with a current `updatedAt`. Persona 2's "Vintage" style and turn-3 options are now values from `OPTION_WHITELISTS.aesthetic_style`.
  - mcp-a2a-routing and mcp-boardroom-collaboration: the 2026-11-19 root cause was right; an earlier 2026-11-21 note here (now replaced) wrongly said these specs did NOT need a real MCP server. `SSEClientTransport` reads tool results from the long-lived SSE stream, which `route.fulfill` closes at once. Fixed with a real local SSE gateway, `e2e/fixtures/mcpSseServer.ts` (same `SSEServerTransport` as `packages/firebase/src/mcp/index.ts`) on the dev endpoint `127.0.0.1:5001`. The auth fixture's Cloud Functions catch-all also matched `:5001`, so each spec lets `**/mcpEndpoint/**` through. The old assertion expected the raw tool payload in chat, but the app marks tool payloads system-only; the specs now assert that the gateway received the call (with the user's arguments) and that the Publicist's message reports "Executed remote tool: generate_playlist_pitch". No seat answers as `manager`; the Conductor (`generalist`) posts the coordination summary.
- **Repair evidence:** local runs: detroit-techno-onboarding 1 passed (4.6m, all 5 personas); mcp-a2a-routing + mcp-boardroom-collaboration 2 passed (29.6s); vitest onboarding/profile/marketing 132 passed. Mock-backed, so structural only (`.agent/REAL_USER_AUTHENTICITY.md`): a real slow-network onboarding run on a genuine account has not been done.
- **MCP stub withdrawn (2026-11-21):** Codex P1 on #982: the local SSE stub (`e2e/fixtures/mcpSseServer.ts`) is a new fake external service, which `.agent/REAL_USER_AUTHENTICITY.md` forbids. It is removed. A genuine run can't happen in CI: the gateway fails closed without a real Arcjet key, needs a verified real account and a release the caller owns, and `generate_playlist_pitch` makes a paid Vertex call; emulators would still need seeded users and an injected token. The two legacy specs are now tagged `@external-legacy @structural` (excluded from `npm run test:e2e`), and the genuine check is `e2e/mcp-publicist-live.spec.ts` (`@live`, sign-in through the visible UI, no mocks). It needs `PLAYWRIGHT_BASE_URL=https://indii.music`, `PRODUCTION_SHA`, `E2E_TEST_EMAIL`/`E2E_TEST_PASSWORD` and `E2E_LIVE_RELEASE_ID`, so only the owner can run it. Closure needs that live pass.
- **Local run tips:** the installed Chromium is build 1243, so use a throwaway config outside git that sets `executablePath: '/opt/pw-browsers/chromium'`, `video: 'off'` and `screenshot: 'off'` (no ffmpeg). Do not run two Playwright jobs at once; they share the dev server on port 4242 and one can kill it.
- **Live MCP run (2026-11-22 00:16 UTC / 2026-11-21 19:16 EST) — BLOCKED, not run to the Boardroom step:** environment https://app.indii.music, reached from https://indii.music; the owner signed in themself in the desktop app's built-in browser (existing account, not created in this run; no plan or tier was shown on the screens visited). `data-build-sha` on `app-container` = `c1f2c2ae6024638aafffc4a4c59b40f6722406ac` (#984), bundle `index-D8O9b5ak.js`. No mocks, route interception, store writes, injected auth or seeded data. Distribution loaded with no console errors and showed "NO ACTIVE RELEASES" ("Delivery Health: No releases yet", 0/4 distributors). The tab labelled "Catalogue" renders the distributor-connections panel (`value="connections"`); the release list is under "New Release". Opening Submit Release showed "No canonical masters found — ingest one first" and "No brand assets found — upload one first"; the form was cancelled without submitting. No release id existed, so no Boardroom prompt was sent, no paid AI call was made, and no gateway POST, Publicist message or `[McpClientService]` console output was produced. Root cause of the block is ISSUE-1692: even a completed Distribution release could not be used, because the release list and the pitch tool read different collections and the web submit path is desktop-only. Next: repair ISSUE-1692, then repeat this run with a release created through the UI.

### ISSUE-1706: Publicist's generate_playlist_pitch declaration uses argument names the server rejects

- **Status:** 🟡 PARTIAL — merged in #998 (`bd5ea577b`); live re-run passed the stated criteria 2026-11-22 (see ISSUE-1691); pitch text not yet read back
- **Severity:** 🔴 CRITICAL (the Publicist's playlist pitch can never succeed)
- **Module:** Agents / `PublicistAgent`, remote MCP `generate_playlist_pitch`
- **Evidence:** live run 2026-11-22 (ISSUE-1691): two tool calls returned `status: failed` with resource id `unknown`. `packages/firebase/src/mcp/tools/generatePlaylistPitch.ts` requires `releaseId` and `targetPlaylist`; `packages/renderer/src/services/agent/definitions/PublicistAgent.ts` declared `trackId` (required) and `pitchAngle`, so the model sent `trackId` and the handler threw at `requireString(args, 'releaseId')`.
- **Fix (branch):** the declaration now carries `releaseId` and `targetPlaylist` (required) and `curatorName`, with descriptions; a test pins it to the server schema.
- **Verification:** `PublicistAgent.test.ts` + agent tools suites 464 passed / 24 skipped; typecheck exit 0; ESLint clean. Live re-run pending deploy.
- **Acceptance:** live Boardroom run shows "Executed remote tool: generate_playlist_pitch" and a grounded draft for a real release, with no "Step failed".

### ISSUE-1707: Create Release wizard: submit spinner never ends; silent cover rejection; asset drop and tools field problems

- **Status:** 🟡 PARTIAL — four of six items merged in #1000 (`b602cb07d`) and checked on production 2026-11-22 (three of them; the submit deadlines need a full submit)
- **Severity:** 🟠 HIGH
- **Module:** Publishing / `ReleaseWizard`, `useDDEXRelease`
- **Evidence:** live run 2026-11-22 (ISSUE-1691), build `e0cae2eba`.
  - After Submit, the record reached `metadata_complete` (catalogue showed it within seconds) but the dialog stayed on "Submitting release… Please wait" for 8+ minutes and never reached the complete step.
  - With a 1276×1276 cover attached, Next stayed disabled on the Assets step with no message saying the cover is under 3000×3000.
  - Dropping a Project Assets tile needs a real browser drag; the tile and drop zone work together only through native DnD, so keyboard and assistive users have no path from Project Assets to the cover slot.
  - Double-clicking a Project Assets tile while the wizard is open opens Creative Canvas and navigates away, and the wizard loses everything entered.
  - The "Autonomous tools used" field strips spaces ("Flow Music (flowmusic.app)" saved as "FlowMusic(flowmusic.app)").
  - The AI-disclosure copy still says "ERN 4.3 Autonomous Content Disclosure", "New DDEX standards", "Intelligence-generated" and "Autonomous tools".
- **Server evidence for the spinner (2026-11-22):** the record `REDACTED` read back from Firestore had `status: metadata_complete`, `updatedAt` 19:10:52Z against `createdAt` 19:06:08Z, no `packagingError`, no `coverArtAuditError`, so the server finished while the client stayed on "Submitting". Which awaited step stalled is not proven (the audit call, the packaging run, or the final status write's acknowledgement are all awaited with no client deadline; `runAgent` itself is bounded at 5 min, which the stall exceeded).
- **Fix (branch):** every awaited step after the draft is created now has a deadline (cover check 90 s, packaging 330 s, final write 30 s) via `withStepDeadline`; the progress view names the step in plain words ("Checking your cover art…", "Packaging your release…", "Finishing up…"); a stalled check or run no longer stamps the record failed and tells the artist the draft is saved; a slow acknowledgement of the final status write no longer blocks completion (Firestore keeps the write queued). The Assets step now shows the cover's reason ("Cover art: …") with "Use Replace Image" once an unusable cover is attached. The tools field keeps what is typed (spaces survived only until the next keystroke before) and the list is derived from it. Disclosure copy is plain ("AI Content Disclosure", "Streaming platforms ask you to say how AI was used…", "AI Tools Used"); the legally relevant "Fully/Partially AI-Generated" wording stays.
- **Remaining two items (branch `claude/wizard-and-canvas-fixes`):** Project Assets now has a pick mode: the wizard registers a request on the Assets step (and a guard for every step while it is open), so clicking an image in Project Assets uses it as cover art (banner "Choose an image for your cover art", aria-label "Use as cover art: …"), an "Or choose from Project Assets" button opens the panel on that tab, and clicking an asset while the wizard is open no longer navigates to the Studio editor (it says to finish or close Create Release). Video tiles are refused for a cover. Tests: 3 new `AssetsPanel` cases, `assetPickRequest` store tests.
- **Verification:** publishing suites 58/58 (new tests: `submitDeadline`, `parseAiTools`); typecheck exit 0; ESLint 0 errors. The stall's root cause is not verified; the next live run will show the named step.
- **Acceptance:** submit closes on completion with the release ID; an undersized cover shows the reason; a non-drag way to pick a Project Assets image exists; opening an asset does not discard the wizard; the tools field keeps spaces; disclosure copy is plain.

- **Production check (2026-11-22, build `b602cb07d`, owner session, no submit so no paid call):** (1) disclosure step shows "AI Content Disclosure" and "Streaming platforms ask you to say how AI was used in making a release." with none of "Autonomous", "DDEX" or "Intelligence-generated"; (2) the tools field kept "Flow Music (flowmusic.app)" with its space after typing it one character at a time; (3) attaching the 1276×1276 cover left Next disabled and showed "Cover art: Image too small. Minimum: 3000x3000px. Current: 1276x1276px" with "Use Replace Image to pick a different file." **Not yet checked:** the submit deadlines and the named progress line, which need a full submit (one paid packaging call).

### ISSUE-1708: Creative Canvas save is slow and downsizes; false unsaved-changes guard; workspace prompt on every load; library upload fails

- **Status:** 🟡 PARTIAL — branch `claude/wizard-and-canvas-fixes`; workspace prompt and slow save not changed; not yet seen on production
- **Severity:** 🟡 MEDIUM
- **Module:** Creative / `CreativeCanvas`; workspace sync; upload queue
- **Evidence:** live run 2026-11-22.
  - "Save Canvas" took about 90 s and stored a 1276×1276 copy of a 3000×3000 artwork.
  - After that save, leaving Creative Studio still raised "Unsaved Changes", and a hard navigation raised the browser's "Leave site?" guard.
  - Each Studio page load asked "A newer workspace from another device is available. Load it now?" (answered Cancel each time).
  - The Upload Queue showed "Assembly Line Halo.wav — Failed to save to cloud library" while the wizard upload of the same file succeeded.
- **Causes found and changes (branch `claude/wizard-and-canvas-fixes`):**
  - Canvas save size: `CanvasOperationsService.saveCanvas()` exported at a fixed 2x of the on-screen artboard, so a 3000×3000 artwork on a normal window saved at ~1276×1276. It now exports at the base image's native resolution (never below the old 2x, longest side capped at 6000 px) via `exportMultiplierFor`.
  - Slow save: not proven (an upload of a ~16 MB PNG plus several Firestore writes, while the Firestore write channel returned 503 and re-connected repeatedly in the same session). The save now logs per-phase timings (`exportedPng`, `blobReady`, `uploaded`, `sessionsPersisted`, `bytes`) so the next run names the slow phase.
  - False unsaved-changes guard: `CreativeStudio` counted any non-empty prompt as unsaved, including one already generated from. Only text typed since the last finished generation (or an active generation) counts; the prompt a generation started with is what gets settled, so edits made while it runs stay unsaved (Codex P2).
  - Workspace prompt on every load: cause found, NOT changed. `useWorkspaceSync` compares the cloud snapshot time with an in-memory push time that is zero on each page load, so a snapshot last written by another device looks newer every time. A first attempt remembered the answered snapshot in localStorage; Codex review (P2 on #1002) correctly showed that skipping the prompt after a reload can leave an empty local workspace marked hydrated and then overwrite the cloud copy, because the store persists only presentation preferences. That change was reverted. The prompt stays until a safe design exists (for example persisting the snapshot itself with the acknowledgement).
  - Library upload: `StorageService` called `fetch()` on a `data:` URL for audio and video, which the production CSP `connect-src` blocks (console: "Cloud upload failed: TypeError: Failed to fetch"; queue: "Failed to save to cloud library"). Data URLs are now decoded locally (`mediaUrlToBlob`).
  - Tests: `exportMultiplierFor` (4), `mediaUrlToBlob` (3).

### ISSUE-1709: Nine remote MCP tools are wired to agents without function declarations

### ISSUE-1710: Boardroom first send fails with "Context preparation timed out during memory recall"

- **Status:** 🟡 PARTIAL — branch `claude/wizard-and-canvas-fixes`; not yet seen on production
- **Severity:** 🟠 HIGH (the first send of most Boardroom sessions fails; the artist must resend several times)
- **Module:** Agents / `ContextPipeline`, `ContextPreparation`
- **Evidence:** live runs 2026-11-22 (ISSUE-1691): the first three sends of each Publicist prompt returned "❌ Error: Context preparation timed out during memory recall. Please retry."; the fourth ran the tool. Earlier history stages ("during conversation history") had been bounded by #989/#990; memory recall had not.
- **Cause:** `ContextPipeline.buildContext` ran memory recall, fallback memories, active plans and product-skill search under one shared 30 s `ContextPreparation` budget, and a deadline in `ContextPreparation.wait` is sticky: after it fires, `preparation.throwIfStopped()` in each stage's "non-blocking" catch rethrows it, so an enrichment that merely ran slow failed the whole turn. Which read was slow in the 2,300-message session was not measured.
- **Fix (branch):** those four reads now use `readOptionalContext` with their own budgets (memory recall 8 s, fallback memories 3 s, active plans 3 s, product skill 3 s); a timeout or failure logs a warning, the turn continues without that context, and when memories were skipped the reply carries "Saved memories are unavailable for this reply." Conversation history and the artist master directive stay required. Stop still cancels immediately (`readOptionalContext` rethrows it; covered by its existing tests).
- **Verification:** agent component suites 31/31; full renderer run 9,126 passed, 2 failed (the known `services/share/milestones.test.ts`, same on unchanged `main`); typecheck exit 0; ESLint 0 errors. No ContextPipeline-level test: the pipeline needs the full store and service graph, so the behavior rests on `readOptionalContext`'s tests plus a live check.
- **Acceptance:** on production, the first Boardroom send after a page load returns a reply (or the memories-unavailable note) instead of the timeout error, in a session with a long history.
